mina: FYI saw a subtle perf regression on canary after yesterday's runtime bump — KV cache hit-rate dropped ~8% for a subset of traffic :thinking_face:

carmen: Oh interesting. Which subset? any correlation to prefix length or model variant?

mina: Appears concentrated on mid-length prompts (30-80 tokens) that share a lot of common conversational prefixes. Heatmap shows many small hotspots across kv shards rather than concentrated keys.

leo: That sounds like a keying/hash distribution problem + eviction churn. Did we change the hashing of prefix keys in the new kernel selection?

mina: We didn't touch hashing directly, but the new kernel selection path (2.2) switches to batched tensor packing that changes request ordering and batch boundaries. That changed KV access patterns — more interleaving across requests -> worse local cache locality.

ryan: Got it. So cache effective working set increased because batches now contain more varied prefixes. Can we prove that from profiles?

mina: Attaching quick profiler excerpt:```
prefetch_hits_by_key_bucket: [0.62, 0.11, 0.09, 0.18]  # top-200 keys vs tail
batch_locality_index: before=0.78 after=0.41
avg_tokens_per_batch: before=18 after=25
```

carmen: Oof. avg_tokens_per_batch increase explains batching heuristics effect. Longer batches hop across conversations so same shard sees more unique keys per batch -> evictions.

leo: We should consider a targeted prefill strategy that biases warmers toward the observed heatmap hotspots instead of uniform synthetic traffic. Basically heatmap-driven scheduled warmers + autoscaler hook on scale events.

mina: Proposed coordinator logic:
- compute weekly heatmap per tenant (prefix hash -> score)
- pick top-N keys with decay window
- schedule warmers during deploy and when autoscaler spins up nodes
- throttle synthetic queries to match typical user distribution

ryan: Looks reasonable. Couple questions: how do we avoid amplifying rare-but-expensive prefixes? Also need to avoid creating synthetic collisions that perturb cache eviction policy.

carmen: Two mitigations: cap per-key QPS from warmers, and add jittered TTLs so we don't synchronize evictions. Also prefer warmers that run single-key, single-tenant priming to avoid cross-tenant interference.

leo: Also add a coordinator mode for canary warmers: run warmers only on canary instances first, measure hit-rate delta and tail-latency before global rollout.

mina: Implementation sketch (cron example):
```bash
# daily job to push top keys to prefill queue
curl -X POST $COORDINATOR_URL/api/prefill -d '{"keys": ["k1","k2",...], "rate": 10}'
```

carmen: Nice. We'll need metrics: prefill.requests, prefill.hits, prefill.per-key-qps, prefill.evictions. Add retention for per-key heatmap for 14 days.

infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: deploy/runtime-2.2 rolled at 2026-03-17T03:21:00Z to canary cluster :rocket:

mina: After canary warmers prototype I ran a 1-hour test on canary cluster: hit-rate up 6.1% on targeted keys, tail P99 decode latency down 12ms, overall token cost unchanged. Small risk: one tenant's distribution pushed eviction noise to others when warmers were cross-tenant.

ryan: Ok enforce single-tenant warmers by default. For autoscaling events, hook into the scale-up lifecycle and prepopulate new nodes with hot keys prior to accepting traffic (use draining window).

leo: We should also add a perf regression guard: if kernel selection changes batch_locality_index by > 20% rollback or adjust batching heuristics automatically. That'd prevent stealth regressions in future.

mina: Agreed. I'll draft a short RFC for the prefill coordinator + canary warmers + autoscaler hook. Plan: prototype on canary, collect prefill.* metrics, iterate.

carmen: Thanks — please include a simple dashboard (heatmap + per-key hist) and an alert for cross-tenant eviction rate spike.

mina: Will do. If anyone has objections to single-tenant default, speak now. Otherwise I'll start the RFC and a small PoC job. :thumbsup:

leo: No objections. Let's keep the synthetic QPS low to start and measure.

ryan: I'll add a unit in the autoscaler lifecycle to call the prefill endpoint before marking nodes ready.

mina: Awesome — creating RFC PR now.
